question:
Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be defined piecewise as $f(x) = \begin{cases}x^2, & x \leq 0 \\ 2x + 1, & 0 < x < 3 \\ (3-x)^2 + 7, & x \geq 3\end{cases}$.

(a) Prove $f$ is a function from $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$; justify that it is well-defined and find the range.

(b) Prove $f$ is neither one-one nor onto, but that it is a bijection from $(-\infty,0]$ to $[0,\infty)$.

(c) For $g(x) = \sqrt{7-x}$, define $h(x) = f(g(x))$. Find the domain and range of $h$.
explanation:

Thus $f$ is a well-defined function.

Range:

For $x \le 0$, $f(x)=x^2$, so the range is $[0,\infty)$.

For $x \ge 3$, $f(x)=(3-x)^2+7$. As $x$ increases, $(3-x)^2$ ranges from $0$ to $\infty$, so the range is $[7,\infty)$.

Combining all ranges gives $[0,\infty)$.

(b) $f$ is not one-one because different inputs can give the same output (for example, values from the square part).

Also $f$ is not onto $\mathbb{R}$ because its outputs are only in $[0,\infty)$.

However, the restriction $f|_{(-\infty,0]}:x \mapsto x^2$ maps $(-\infty,0]$ onto $[0,\infty)$ and is one-one on that domain.

Hence it is a bijection from $(-\infty,0]$ to $[0,\infty)$.

(c) $g(x)=\sqrt{7-x}$.

Domain: $7-x \ge 0 \Rightarrow x \le 7$. Thus domain of $g$ is $(-\infty,7]$. Range of $g$ is $[0,\infty)$.

Let $t=g(x) \ge 0$. Then $h(x)=f(t)$.

If $0 \le t < 3$, then $f(t)=2t+1 \in [1,7)$.

If $t \ge 3$, then $f(t)=(3-t)^2+7 \ge 7$.

Hence the range of $h$ is $[1,\infty)$.

options.A:
(a) $f$ is not well-defined.
(b) $f$ is bijective on $\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$.
(c) Domain of $h$ is $\mathbb{R}$ and range is $\mathbb{R}$.
options.B:
(a) $f$ is well-defined and range is $\mathbb{R}$.
(b) $f$ is one-one and onto.
(c) Domain of $h$ is $[7,\infty)$ and range is $[0,\infty)$.
options.C:
(a) $f$ is well-defined and its range is $[0,\infty)$.
(b) $f$ is neither one-one nor onto $\mathbb{R}$, but its restriction from $(-\infty,0]$ to $[0,\infty)$ is bijective.
(c) Domain of $h$ is $(-\infty,7]$ and range of $h$ is $[1,\infty)$.
options.D:

(b) $f$ is one-one but not onto.
